tfa.admin.posture_all_full: All factors at full credit — well done.
tfa.admin.backup_explainer: Download a snapshot of your plugin configuration so you can restore it on another server or roll back after a misconfiguration.
tfa.admin.restore_explainer: Paste an exported JSON envelope below. Encrypted exports prompt for the passphrase. Imports overwrite the live configuration — download a fresh export first.

tfa.setup.scan_qr: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
tfa.setup.enter_code: Enter the 6-digit code shown by the app to confirm.
tfa.setup.invalid_code: That code didn't match. Try again.

tfa.challenge.locked_out: Too many failed attempts. Try again later.
tfa.challenge.expired: This challenge has expired. Sign in again.
tfa.challenge.enroll_copy: Your server requires two-factor authentication before this account can continue. Set up an authenticator app now.
tfa.challenge.enroll_code_label: Enter the 6-digit code from your app
tfa.challenge.trust_device: Trust this device (skip 2FA for future logins)
tfa.challenge.hint_passkey_only: Use your registered passkey to continue.
tfa.challenge.hint_enroll_continue: The account will continue into Jellyfin after the first code is confirmed.
tfa.challenge.hint_recovery: Each recovery code works once. Save the others somewhere safe.
tfa.challenge.email_input_label: Enter the 6-digit code sent to your email
tfa.challenge.totp_input_label: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app
tfa.challenge.hint_email: Email codes expire 5 minutes after they are sent.
tfa.challenge.email_send_failed: Failed to send email code. Too many requests?
tfa.challenge.validation_recovery_format: Enter a recovery code (10 chars, letters + digits).
tfa.challenge.passkey_no_auth_response: Verified, but no auth response — sign in again.
tfa.disable.title: Disable two-factor authentication
tfa.disable.warning: This will remove all 2FA factors for your account. Your account will be protected only by your password.
tfa.disable.requires_code: Enter a current 2FA code to confirm this change.
tfa.stepup.title: Sensitive action
tfa.stepup.explainer: Confirm with a current 2FA code before continuing.
tfa.stepup.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
tfa.error.unknown: Something went wrong. Check the server log.
tfa.admin.common.api_keys_note: Service integrations like Sonarr/Radarr use standard Jellyfin API keys, which already bypass user authentication — no plugin configuration needed.
tfa.admin.overview.load_failed: Failed to load dashboard. Check the server log.
tfa.admin.overview.no_chart_data: No data in the last 30 days
tfa.admin.users.heading: User 2FA Status
tfa.admin.users.confirm_force_logout: Force-logout this user? All their Jellyfin sessions are terminated and trust state is cleared.
tfa.admin.users.confirm_revoke_all: Revoke EVERY trusted browser, paired device, registered device id and app password for this user? They will need to re-do 2FA on every client.
tfa.admin.devices.heading: All Trusted Devices
tfa.admin.devices.explainer: Devices that bypass 2FA. Revoke any you don't recognize.
tfa.admin.devices.confirm_revoke_all: Revoke EVERY trusted browser for this user?
tfa.admin.pairings.heading: TV / Limited-Input Devices
tfa.admin.pairings.quick_connect_note:
Recommended flow: Jellyfin Quick Connect. On the TV, choose Quick Connect. Then on a 2FA-verified phone or laptop, open Jellyfin and approve the displayed code. The TV will sign in and inherit the verified status — no TOTP prompt on the TV itself.

Make sure Quick Connect is enabled in Jellyfin's Dashboard → Quick Connect.
tfa.admin.pairings.manual_explainer: Pending requests from devices that can't use Quick Connect. Approve to grant a 30-day trusted device.
tfa.admin.audit.heading: Login Audit Log
tfa.admin.audit.filter_placeholder: Filter by user, IP, device, result...
tfa.admin.diagnostics.heading: Plugin Diagnostics
tfa.admin.diagnostics.explainer: Run a checklist of common configuration / state checks. Re-run after changing settings or a Jellyfin upgrade.
tfa.admin.trips.heading: Recent Rate-Limit Trips
tfa.admin.trips.explainer: Per-bucket rate-limit hits since last restart. A burst here usually means someone is brute-forcing — or the limit is too tight for legitimate use.
tfa.admin.sso.heading: OIDC / SSO Providers
tfa.admin.sso.note: Add an external identity provider (Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Apple, Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak, PocketID, Cloudflare Access, or any OIDC-compliant IdP). Users get a "Sign in with X" button on the login page. Each provider needs its own OAuth client registered at the IdP — set the redirect URI to /TwoFactorAuth/Oidc/Callback/<providerId> on this server.
tfa.admin.sso.empty: No providers yet. Click "Add provider" to set one up.
tfa.admin.sso.confirm_delete: Delete this OIDC provider? Users linked to it will lose the link.
tfa.admin.sso.ph_client_secret: (leave blank when editing to keep existing)
tfa.admin.sso.opt_auto_create: Auto-create Jellyfin users on first sign-in (only enable for trusted IdPs)
tfa.admin.sso.opt_require_mfa: Require IdP MFA (refuse sign-in if amr claim doesn't show MFA)
tfa.admin.sso.opt_bypass_2fa: Skip plugin 2FA (recommended — IdP already authenticated the user)
tfa.admin.bans.heading: Active IP Bans
tfa.admin.bans.note: Source IPs are auto-banned after the configured threshold of failed sign-ins (see Settings → Brute-Force Protection). LAN, trusted-proxy, and exempt CIDRs are never banned.
tfa.admin.settings.scope_optional: Optional — users opt in from Setup page
tfa.admin.settings.scope_admins: Admins only — only Jellyfin admins must have 2FA
tfa.admin.settings.scope_help: v2.4: per-role policy. Admins-only is the standard pattern for shared media servers.
tfa.admin.settings.opt_hibp: Check passwords against Have I Been Pwned on sign-in
tfa.admin.settings.hibp_help: v2.4: opt-in. Only the first 5 hex chars of SHA-1(password) leave the server (k-anonymity). On a breach hit, an audit-log entry is written and a warning is logged — sign-in is never blocked. Fails open if api.pwnedpasswords.com is unreachable.
tfa.admin.settings.smtp_explainer: Required if you enable email OTP. Test with a real provider before relying on it.
tfa.admin.settings.lbl_issuer: Issuer name shown in users' apps
tfa.admin.settings.issuer_help: Existing enrollments keep their old name. New enrollments will use this. Pick something users will recognize as your server.
tfa.admin.settings.lbl_alert_emails: Admin email addresses for security alerts (one per line)
tfa.admin.settings.lbl_webhook_url: Webhook URL (POST every event as JSON)
tfa.admin.settings.suspicious_note: Resolve sign-in IPs to ASN + country via MaxMind GeoLite2 .mmdb files. Sign in once with a free MaxMind account, download GeoLite2-ASN and GeoLite2-Country, place the .mmdb files inside Jellyfin's config directory, and paste the absolute paths below. Without these the plugin still works — just no first-seen alerts.
tfa.admin.settings.bruteforce_note: Auto-bans source IPs that exceed the failure threshold across all users. LAN bypass and trusted-proxy CIDRs are always exempt. Active bans appear under the IP Bans tab.
tfa.admin.settings.lbl_ban_exempt: Exempt CIDRs (one per line — never banned)
tfa.admin.settings.travel_note: Alerts when consecutive sign-ins for the same user are physically impossible given elapsed time (e.g., London then Tokyo 30 min apart). Requires a GeoLite2-City.mmdb database — without it, suspicious-login alerts still work on ASN/country alone.
tfa.admin.settings.lbl_travel_kmh: Max plausible speed (km/h, default 900 ≈ jet cruise)
tfa.admin.settings.webauthn_note: Most setups can leave these blank — RP ID and origin are derived from the request. Override only when behind a reverse proxy whose public hostname differs from the internal one.
tfa.admin.settings.lbl_max_sess: Default max concurrent sessions per user (0 = unlimited)
tfa.admin.settings.opt_hairpin: Treat server's own public IP as LAN (NAT hairpin) — see security note
tfa.admin.settings.hairpin_help: Anyone sharing the same WAN egress (other devices on the same router, including IoT or guest WiFi) bypasses 2FA. Off by default.
tfa.admin.settings.saved_partial_stepup: Other settings saved; hardening config requires step-up verification.
tfa.admin.settings.saved_with_hardening_: Settings saved (hardening config endpoint error — check server log)
tfa.admin.hardening.heading: Hardening (v2.5.0)
tfa.admin.hardening.opt_require_to_disab: Require authenticator/recovery code before a user can turn off their own 2FA
When enabled, users must supply a current TOTP code or a recovery code before they can disable their own two-factor authentication. Admins are unaffected.
tfa.admin.hardening.stepup_config: All config changes — any admin settings save
tfa.admin.hardening.stepup_level_help: Controls which admin actions require a fresh 2FA code from the performing admin. "Off" restores v2.4 behaviour. Saved through the gated /TwoFactorAuth/Admin/HardeningConfig endpoint.
tfa.admin.backup.prompt_passphrase: Set a passphrase (>=8 chars). You will need this exact passphrase to restore.
tfa.admin.backup.passphrase_too_short: Passphrase must be at least 8 characters
tfa.admin.lang.heading: Language
tfa.admin.lang.explainer: Change the language of the plugin UI for your own account. The admin can set a server-wide default in the Hardening section.
tfa.admin.modal.title: Admin authentication required
tfa.admin.modal.body: This action requires a fresh verification code from your authenticator app (or a recovery code).
tfa.admin.modal.err_too_many: Too many attempts. Try again later.
